export const meta = {
  name: 'audit-picks-apply',
  description: "Apply Eric's accepted picks from the 2026-10-25 audit sweep: ~/.claude work serially, outside work serially, shadow-log review read-only",
  phases: [
    { title: 'Apply', detail: '2 serial fixers on disjoint trees + 1 read-only reviewer' },
  ],
}

const HANDOFF = '~/DEV/docs/handoffs/2026-10-25-audit-sweep-all-domains.md'
const AUDIT = '~/.claude/audits/2026-10-22-system-audit-findings.md'
const COMMON = `
Eric accepted the agent's pick on each item below ("all picks", 2026-10-25). The full option text for each id is in ${HANDOFF} under "Eric decisions"; the evidence and original fix are under the same id's heading in ${AUDIT}. Read both before acting on an item.
House rules:
- Never print secret values, tokens, keys, or athlete/health data (names, injuries, body composition). Count or name files only.
- Never open contents of DexaProject, SpecialRequests/TOS_ES, or Linda_Projects beyond its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md first lines.
- Never read or walk files through the Google Drive FUSE mount; use the gws CLI for Drive (gws is the default for any Google API work).
- Never run \`memsearch index\` by hand. Never upgrade or reinstall pwsh/PowerShell (launchd wrapper trap).
- Shared hooks: edit only ~/.claude/hooks (~/.codex/hooks links there).
- Never delete with rm. Move to ~/.Trash/<name>-2026-10-25. Drive deletes go to Drive Trash via gws (files update --params with trashed true), never permanent delete.
- Football season is on: do not change live football/CFB pipelines or schedules.
- Read every file before editing; smallest change; match style. Run the repo tests touched (python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_*.py; pytest via ~/.local/bin/uv run --with pytest pytest -q; pwsh test files where present).
- Commit per repo, only the files you changed (never git add -A in ~/.claude; other sessions may have uncommitted work). Do NOT commit ${AUDIT} or ${HANDOFF}; the caller records status. End every commit message with exactly:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013cwnYrAYa2PQ3pgLjQbq1g
Push after committing.
- If a step turns out riskier than the pick described, or a precondition fails, skip it and say why. Do not improvise a different option.`

const RESULT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    results: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string' },
          outcome: { type: 'string', enum: ['done', 'skipped', 'failed', 'needs-eric'] },
          commit: { type: 'string', description: 'repo + short sha(s), or empty' },
          note: { type: 'string', description: 'one or two sentences: what changed and the check/test result, or why not' },
        },
        required: ['id', 'outcome', 'commit', 'note'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['results'],
}

phase('Apply')
const [inside, outside, shadow] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${COMMON}

You own everything under ~/.claude (dotclaude repo, ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler, ~/.claude/skills). Nobody else edits there in this run. Do the items in this order:

1. ids disksec-github-pat-in-pushed-transcript + backups-secrets-in-tracked-transcripts (one change): a WARN-ONLY secret check in ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 that runs before the dotclaude commit, scans the staged projects/ files with the script's existing secret regex, and writes matching FILE NAMES only (never values) to ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log and the backup log. It must never block or fail the backup. Add an offline test in the existing daily-backup test file. No history purge.
2. id backups-dexa-via-fuse-to-exfat, pick B (no spare encrypted disk exists): remove DexaProject from the SSD layer in ~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json so nothing reads it through the Drive mount. Validate the JSON loads and run the backup script's dry-run/offline test if one exists.
3. id mp-health-data-in-compiler-stores, pick (a) going forward only: add a rule to the flush and compile prompts ("never record athlete names with medical, injury or body-composition details; refer to them by role") and a regex warning in flush.py. Then list the existing daily-log/article FILES that match health keywords, by name only, in your note (no content). Do not scrub them.
4. id mp-recompile-on-append, pick (a): stop the compile step; keep flush and the daily logs; leave the existing articles frozen. Find where compile is triggered (flush.py end-of-day trigger, launchd, jobs.json) and turn off only the compile trigger, with a comment saying why (cost vs use, Eric 2026-10-25). Make sure session-start still works and tests pass.
5. id mp-windows-slug-stale-indexed, pick (a), WITH A PRECONDITION: the Windows laptop is still used for desktop-app sessions. First check the newest mtime of any file in ~/.claude/projects/C--Users-*/memory/. If any file there changed after 2026-10-14, SKIP with outcome needs-eric and give the folder names and dates. Otherwise move the C--Users-* memory folders to ~/.claude/_windows-import-archive/ and drop them from recall.py's glob; run recall.py tests. Do not run memsearch index.
6. Settings LAST, one edit of ~/.claude/settings.json (back up first to ~/.claude/backups/settings.json.pre-picks-2026-10-25):
   - id disksec-auto-mode-python-allow, pick (a): remove the blanket python/python3 allow rules and any remaining Windows-path rules; add deny rules Bash(rm -rf:*) and Edit/Write denies for ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.local.json (use the exact rule syntax Claude Code documents; check existing rule formats in the file).
   - id settings-hooks-bare-bash-allow, pick A: remove Bash(launchctl:*) and Bash(git:*); set skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt to false. Keep the other interpreter rules.
   - id spm-superpowers-overrides-ineffective, pick A: set enabledPlugins "superpowers@claude-plugins-official" to false.
   Write with python (json, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, trailing newline). Check: the JSON loads, \`claude --version\` runs, git diff shows only the intended lines. Commit.
Return one result per id (use both ids for item 1).`, { label: 'apply:inside-claude', phase: 'Apply', schema: RESULT_SCHEMA }),

  () => agent(`${COMMON}

You own everything OUTSIDE ~/.claude (~/DEV repos, ~/.zshrc, ~/.gemini, Homebrew, npm, Drive via gws, files in ~). Never edit files under ~/.claude. Do the items in order:

1. id disksec-skill-button-closeout-bypass, pick (a): drop closeout from the skill-button BUTTONS list and from the docs (the handoff names COMMANDS.md:395 and SKILL-BUTTONS.md:16 and :42; find the BUTTONS file with grep under ~/DEV). Leave forecast-capture and every other button unchanged. Run that repo's tests if any.
2. id backups-local-only-folders-in-cloud-mirror, pick A: make the first line of ~/DEV/Linda_Projects/CLAUDE.md carry the "local only" marker that ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py looks for (read cloud-push.py's check to match it exactly; read only the first lines of that CLAUDE.md). Commit and push in that repo. Then confirm with a dry check (call cloud-push.py's own local-only function from python, without running a push) that Linda_Projects is now skipped. Then move the Drive folder _MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/Linda_Projects to Drive Trash with gws (find its id with gws; never via the mount).
3. id gaps-antigravity-unguarded, pick A: in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json set toolPermission to ask and allowNonWorkspaceAccess to false (back the file up first next to it as .pre-2026-10-25, outside git). Validate the JSON.
4. id gaps-bypass-aliases: change only the cx alias to sandboxed 'codex --full-auto' (pick A for cx). Leave cc unchanged (Eric's pick allowed either; keep his habit). Find the alias in ~/.zshrc or files it sources; back up the file first; check with zsh -n.
5. id gaps-parked-zip-health-data, pick A: first read the README/notes that say these copies were hash-checked against the live copies; if that claim is missing, skip. Then mv ~/DEV_backup_2026-09-09.zip (or the zip the finding names), ~/Restore and ~/handoff-staging to ~/.Trash/<name>-2026-10-25. Leave the LIFEOS folders and dotclaude-windows-import where they are. Do not open the contents. Make sure no process has files open there (lsof +D is fine on small dirs; otherwise just check ps for anything referencing the path).
6. id mac-brew-npm-outdated, pick (a): \`brew upgrade --dry-run gh git openssl@3 sqlite\` first; if powershell/pwsh appears anywhere in the list, stop and skip. Otherwise run it. Then uninstall the unused npm globals opencode-ai and pi-coding-agent (keep gemini-cli). Check gh --version and git --version still work.
Return one result per id.`, { label: 'apply:outside', phase: 'Apply', schema: RESULT_SCHEMA }),

  () => agent(`${COMMON}

READ-ONLY. id settings-hooks-shadow-gate-unreviewed, pick (A): review the permission shadow-gate log (find the PreToolUse shadow entry in ~/.claude/settings.json and the log it writes, likely ~/.claude/permission-gate/shadow.jsonl). Report counts only plus a sanitized sample: total entries, date range, verdict/decision counts, top tool names, how often the gate would have blocked something that ran, and 5 example entries reduced to tool name + a short generic description (never raw command bodies, paths with names, or secret-looking strings). End with a recommendation: promote the gate (enforce), or retire it, in 2 options max with your pick. Do not edit anything. Return a single result with outcome done and the review in note (note may be long here: up to ~15 lines).`, { label: 'review:shadow-gate', phase: 'Apply', schema: RESULT_SCHEMA }),
])

return { inside: inside && inside.results, outside: outside && outside.results, shadow: shadow && shadow.results }

inside.note: Added Get-StagedSecretFiles to daily-backup.ps1. It runs after git add -A for dotclaude only, scans the staged projects/ files with $SecretRe (moved to script scope and shared with Snapshot-ShellDotfiles), and writes file names only to the backup log and .errors.log. It never adds a $Errors entry, so the backup cannot fail on it. One change beyond the pick: I added github_pat_ to the regex because the leaked PAT had that shape, so the dotfiles refusal is also a little stricter. The new offline test in test_daily_backup.ps1 checks the right names are found, no secret value is logged, it never blocks, and it does not throw outside a repo; the whole suite passes. No history purge. Expect the first nightly run to warn on 1-3 of today's -Users-kristinarash-DEV transcripts: they quote the regex and the test's fake ghp_ token. That is the scan working, not a leak.

Done in the same change as disksec-github-pat-in-pushed-transcript: a warn-only scan before the nightly dotclaude commit that writes file names (never values) to .errors.log and never blocks. The test_daily_backup.ps1 suite passes. History is kept, as pick A says.

Removed the DexaProject entry from backup-manifest.json. The file still loads (138 paths, 0 Dexa) and nothing reads Dexa through the Drive mount now. The offline pwsh suite passes; I did not run a real -DryRun because it fetches four repos and writes to the live log. The copy already on CRASHBOX is still there because backups only add, so 'Drive is the only copy' is true from now on only; Eric must remove the old folder by hand if he wants that. RESTORE.md:66 still describes the CRASHBOX copy; not edited.

Added the 'never record athlete names with medical, injury or body-composition details; refer to them by role' rule to both the flush and compile prompts. flush.py now logs a count-only warning to flush.log when health words appear, and never blocks writing the log; the new test test_flush_health_warning.py and all other compiler tests pass. Nothing was scrubbed. Files matching post-op|ACL|concussion|injur|return-to-competition|RTP|dexa|body comp (a wider set than the handoff's 27): 113 total. 32 are daily logs, by date: 04-14, 06-05, 06-09, 06-10, 06-14, 06-17, 06-18, 06-19, 06-24, 06-25, 07-10, 07-13, 07-22, 09-09, 09-14, 09-16, 09-22, 09-25, 09-26, 09-30, 10-02, 10-03, 10-04, 10-05, 10-06, 10-07, 10-08, 10-10, 10-14, 10-20, 10-24, 10-25. 81 are under knowledge/, including index.md, index.md.bak-20261023 and log.md. One slug is built from an athlete's name: concepts/<athlete-name>-cmj-rtc-reports.md. The rest are project slugs, e.g. concepts/athlete-monitoring-rtp-presentation, hpi-rtp-manual-gap-audit, rtp-clinic-deliverable-finalization, surgery-nlp-extraction, clinical-note-nlp-clustering, ath-medicine-project, skylar-free s2/tezino/spring-exit notes, and connections/dont-baseline-on-the-injured-state, vald-forcedecks-cmj-data-across-projects, athlete-monitoring-communication-grammar. A names-only copy of the full list is at ~/.Trash/hk-list-2026-10-25.txt.

flush.py was the only thing that started compile automatically (no launchd or jobs.json entry runs it). It is now off with COMPILE_ON_FLUSH = False and a comment giving the reason (cost vs use, Eric 2026-10-25). Flush and the daily logs carry on, knowledge/ stays frozen, and running compile.py by hand still works. I did not use scripts/DISABLE because the weekly adjudicate job checks it too. Tests: the compiler tests pass (pipeline 58/58), plus a new check that a good flush starts no compile; session-start.py exits 0 and still prints the article count (540). Not fixed: the weekly lint orphan_source warnings and the health.py compile_backlog count will grow every Sunday (neither writes to .errors.log). The memory notes project_automation-cadence.md and project_memory-compiler-pipeline.md still describe the 18:00 compile.

Skipped: the precondition failed. C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-KeystoneOS/memory changed 2026-10-24 00:52 (1 file, commit 22ea1ba, the de-identify commit), and C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV/memory changed 2026-10-19 15:22 (9 files since 10-14, commit fc53351 'mac memory mirror'). The other 10 C--Users-* memory folders are dated 2026-10-11 or earlier. Both changes look like Mac-side edits rather than the laptop writing, but the precondition is literal, so Eric decides. Nothing moved, recall.py unchanged, no index run.

Removed the 5 blanket python allow rules; no Windows-path rules were left in settings.json. Added deny rules Bash(rm -rf:*), Edit(~/.claude/settings.json) and Edit(~/.claude/settings.local.json). I added no separate Write(...) rules because the docs say Edit rules cover every built-in file-editing tool; Eric can add them if he wants both. The JSON loads, claude --version runs (2.1.310), and the git diff shows only the intended lines. Backup is at ~/.claude/backups/settings.json.pre-picks-2026-10-25 (gitignored; .gitignore:49 says no loose config copies, so it can be deleted once Eric is happy). settings.local.json was not opened or changed; the audit says it holds Bash(powershell.exe:*).

Removed Bash(launchctl:*) and Bash(git:*) and set skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt to false. The other interpreter rules (node, npm, uv run and so on) are kept. Done in the same settings edit and checks as disksec-auto-mode-python-allow; the allow list went from 59 to 52 rules.

Set enabledPlugins superpowers@claude-plugins-official to false in the same settings edit; the 9 superpowers:* skillOverrides keys were left alone. Not done (not in this run's assignment): turning off the synced superpowers copy on claude.ai (spm-unused-enabled-plugins). Both repos are pushed: dotclaude and claude-memory-compiler show main...origin/main.

outside.note: Removed the closeout button line and changed 'Four skills' to 'Three skills' in ~/DEV/COMMANDS.md, then pushed; the repo has no tests to run. The BUTTONS list (~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh:25) and SKILL-BUTTONS.md :16/:42 live under ~/.claude, so I left them untouched and the ~/.claude owner still has to drop closeout there.

Line 1 of Linda_Projects/CLAUDE.md is now '# Linda_Projects — local only', the same marker TOS_ES uses, with @AGENTS.md on line 2; I called cloud-push.py's private_dir() without running a push and it returns True for Linda_Projects and TOS_ES and False for a control folder. I moved Drive _MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/Linda_Projects (id 1nlhO30svMnfCY7kOrITe98wGCZbTWLmt, found by checking each parent id in the path) to Drive Trash with gws, and Drive returned trashed:true.

I backed up the file to settings.json.pre-2026-10-25 (cp -p, mode 600) and set allowNonWorkspaceAccess to false; the JSON loads. agy has no 'ask' value (its help lists always-proceed, request-review, strict, proceed-in-sandbox), so I set toolPermission to request-review, its 'requires your approval before running' mode; I did not launch agy to test it, and artifactReviewPolicy is still always-proceed.

Precondition failed: codex-cli 0.162.1 rejects --full-auto ('unexpected argument', exit 2), so making that change would break cx; ~/.zshrc is unchanged and cc was left as is. The sandboxed choices from codex --help are --approve-for-me, '-s workspace-write -a on-request', or '-s workspace-write -a never'; Eric needs to pick one.

I moved ~/_PARKED_COPIES/DEV_backup_2026-09-09.zip, Restore and handoff-staging to ~/.Trash/<name>-2026-10-25 after lsof and ps showed nothing using them; I did not open their contents, and LIFEOS-v6.0.5, config-LIFEOS and dotclaude-windows-import are still in place. The README makes the check claim, but it says what remains is 'byte-identical to canonical or same name+size', which is weaker than a full hash check; ~/DEV_archive_hold was not part of this pick and was not touched.

I skipped the brew upgrade because it was riskier than the pick said. The dry run would also upgrade 6 dependents, including node and python@3.14 (which the pick said to leave until after the season, and which affects board.py's Cellar path), and it lists openssl@3 going from 3.6.4 to 3.5.9, a downgrade; powershell was not in the list. I removed the npm globals opencode-ai and @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (120 packages, neither was running), kept gemini-cli, and gh 2.100.0 and git 2.55.0 still run.

shadow.note:
Read-only review, nothing edited. The hook is the PreToolUse entry in ~/.claude/settings.json (matcher Bash|PowerShell|mcp__.*|WebFetch|SendMessage|SendUserFile|Artifact). It runs ~/.claude/permission-gate/shadow_hook.py and appends to shadow.jsonl, which is now 6.6 MB, mode 600.
Counts: 21,859 entries plus 1 unparseable line, 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-25, 191 sessions. Growth was about 6.2k lines in the 3 days since the audit and about 1,100 a day in week 43. Verdicts: residue 13,987 (64%), run 7,449, review 376, block 47. Residue share is rising: 61% in week 39, 68% in week 43. Egress calls: 1,418, of which about 850 landed in residue.
Top tools: Bash 18,563, PowerShell 1,341, firecrawl_search 270, context-mode ctx_execute 199, zotero-research search tools 323, chrome computer 156, firecrawl_scrape 144, remote send_message 80, WebFetch 60.
Would it have stopped calls that ran? Every logged call ran, because shadow mode never blocks. Enforcing it would have hard-blocked 47 calls (0.2%) and prompted on 376 (1.7%). For 64% of calls the rules give no verdict, so enforcement would either auto-run those or add about 14k prompts in 5 weeks.
The 47 blocks: 34 are git push, 43 are Bash with egress true, and only 2 show a sensitive folder name in the sanitized shape. In the other 45 the match was in text the sanitizer removed. They fit the 09-22 finding ('folder names in prose'), so they look like false positives, but the sanitized shapes cannot confirm that. Zero true positives were confirmed.
The 376 reviews are mostly rm -f/-rf, git branch -d/-D, git checkout --, Remove-Item -Recurse and Stop-Process. dcg already guards these.
What makes up residue: 8,540 calls are programs the rules don't list (cd plus python, for, sed or awk), 2,032 are loops, 1,138 are heredocs, 735 are inline python and 577 are write redirects. So a v2 rule set would mostly widen the allowlist rather than add safety.
Sanitizer gap (not fixed, read-only): sanitize.py strips only ' -m "..."', so commit messages given with -am, -qam or -qm reach the log verbatim. One block entry carries one. Also, its HOME regex matches only the Windows user path, so Mac paths keep the account folder name.
Samples, described not quoted:
(1) Bash, block L1: cd into a project, git add, commit, push; the trigger was a sensitive folder name in removed text.
(2) Bash, block L1: delete a local branch, then push the remote branch delete.
(3) PowerShell, block L1: write a here-string to files with Set-Content; the egress keyword was inside removed content.
(4) Bash, review L2: cd into a project, then a recursive rm of a temp folder.
(5) Bash, residue: cd into a project, then an inline python heredoc with output redirected.
Recommendation:
(1) PICK: retire. Remove the PreToolUse shadow entry and leave shadow.jsonl in place as frozen Jev evidence; rotation stops mattering once writes stop. Close the 'Watch the shadow log' item at TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md:455.
(2) Promote later, and only after a pre-registered v2 rules.py has run another shadow period with residue well under 20%. v2 means L1 on path arguments only plus the cheap additions listed in STATUS.md. Promoting as-is is not workable at 64% residue.
